title: Intervention-surface lockout breaks recursive self-intervention closure

scientific_object.broad_claim: Recursive/self-referential agents can improve their own scaffold or tools.
scientific_object.narrow_claim: When the capability used for self-reading, self-writing, and self-verification itself enters the fault domain, under what conditions does read-write-verify recursive closure break, and can a strictly bounded out-of-band repair side-channel restore that closure?

canonical_object_qualification.decision: Do not inherit closest-work, substrate, promotion, or scientific lineage from SHADOW-RSI-C01. The current lockout formulation must first be explicitly bound as a new canonical scientific object or assigned a distinct candidate identity.

closest_work_boundary.qualification_rule: Strict closest-work review is admissible only after the reviewed claim is bound to a canonical scientific object. A shadow-only formulation cannot earn novelty authority by literature review alone.
historical_exploratory_scan_only: DGM: recursive code self-modification and inherited self-modification capability
SICA: coding agent edits itself using coding tools
POLARIS: inspect policy/traces, produce persistent policy patch, continue
Self-Harness: prompts, tools, and execution harness are mutable optimization objects
runtime tool-failure benchmarks: availability denial, silent no-op, corrupted state, schema mismatch, retry/fallback/verification
closest_work_boundary.unqualified_hypothesized_intersection: The intervention capability responsible for self-inspection, self-modification, or self-verification is itself the faulted resource, rather than an ordinary task tool.

substrate.qualification_rule: Same-substrate qualification starts only after a canonical scientific object and its closest-work boundary are frozen; otherwise substrate work is engineering feasibility only.
why_close: The source tree is mounted into the agent sandbox at /workspace/exo and is intended to be readable and modifiable by the agent.
Canonical event history is host-side/outside the sandbox and survives ordinary restart/rewind, giving an external lineage domain.
The default harness exposes shell-class execution plus a host-side rebuild/restart capability, so self-intervention is a real multi-path capability surface rather than a single write_file tool.
The project is actively discussing canonical writer/harness identity when harness mutability is allowed, which is adjacent to the recursive trust boundary required here.

dry_run.scientific_interpretation: The dry-run falsifies tool-name and chmod-style W lockout as capability boundaries and establishes that a resource-level read-only boundary can block the enumerated W-equivalent paths. It does not establish full recursive closure lockout because R and V remain unqualified.

promotion_gates.pass_rule: Bind the exact intervention-surface-lockout claim to one canonical scientific object with unique lineage. A reused numeric suffix or a shadow-only branch is insufficient.
promotion_gates.current_result: Canonical SHADOW-RSI-C01 is a different successor-as-improver object and is already terminal STOP_EXACT_REDUCTION_SUPPORTED; no canonical match exists for the current lockout formulation.

promotion_gates.pass_rule: After G0 passes, enumerate functionally equivalent R/W/V paths and demonstrate that the full-lockout arm cannot bypass the intended fault through shell, interpreters, patch/git plumbing, tool-management state, rebuild/restart, or another host API.
promotion_gates.current_result: The W resource-boundary dry-run remains useful engineering evidence only; it grants no scientific or substrate qualification while G0 fails.

promotion_gates.pass_rule: After G0 passes, the modified harness/code must persist across generations while checkpoint, lineage, and evaluator remain outside the fault domain; the supervisor may only restore a predeclared primitive and may not author the repair.

After G0-G2 pass, no-fault sustains R-to-W-to-V; intervention-surface lockout collapses closure; the minimal out-of-band primitive restores it; fixed-agent, history-only reflection, and hidden redundant-tool controls do not recover equally.
